features.name: Portable runner
features.outcome: A user can run an ordinary verification command locally or through an optional runner provider by changing one placement option, and receives the same canonical session either way

features.name: Native execution session reporting
features.outcome: Each explicitly selected reporter receives live execution facts, the session reporter also receives the persisted terminal session, and each resumes delivery without rebuilding work

features.name: Workspace discovery and selection
features.outcome: A user can find the workspace and its projects, then select the exact project, scope, target, or impacted closure intended for a command

features.name: Context and MCP discovery
features.outcome: A user or agent can discover workspace structure and project context through public CLI and MCP surfaces that share one authority, and an extension can contribute a workspace-answering tool without re-deriving any of it

features.name: Job planning and execution
features.outcome: A user can select public jobs, preview their dependency plan, execute them through one engine, and receive a stable result

features.name: Diagnostics and results
features.outcome: A user or agent can diagnose a failed or unsafe run from structured diagnostics, doctor guidance, session reports, and stable exit outcomes, and can collect and summarize the recorded sessions before a disposable worktree takes them with it

features.name: Canonical workspace guidance
features.outcome: A new contributor can discover the supported commands, choose the correct validation gate, use MCP appropriately, and recover from failures using generated and public guidance

features.name: Agent workflow lifecycle
features.outcome: A workspace that opts into an extension's agent content receives the files of the extension release it pinned through init, install and upgrade, and never loses a file it owns

features.name: SDD extraction parity
features.outcome: The extracted SDD surfaces answer byte-for-byte what the built-in CLI answered before deletion, and the extension binary knows the workspace only through the wire

features.name: Reproducible toolchain lock
features.outcome: Install pins, for each toolchain an installed extension answers for, an exact release and each platform's verified archive

features.name: CI document
features.outcome: A repository declares in one reviewed file the commands its CI runs, and the guidance the CLI generates names them as the gate

features.name: Versions derived from git
features.outcome: A user gets the exact version every version line is at, derived from the line's git tags and the conventional commits that touch it

features.name: Distribution channels
features.outcome: A user moves the CLI, the extensions, and the framework dependencies onto a distribution channel through the registries the workspace declares, with the credential that channel needs

features.name: Deploy environments
features.outcome: A user synchronizes a declared environment on the release set its channel points at, with each workload receiving the exact members it owns

features.name: Lazy workspace initialization
features.outcome: A fresh worktree provides its workspace graph to MCP without a full installation, while installation restores independent artifacts concurrently and reports completed actions compactly

features.name: Lock-pinned extension runtime toolchains
features.outcome: An extension prepares its runtime and runs its tasks with the exact toolchain the workspace lock pins, and results are keyed under that identity

features.name: Engine provenance
features.outcome: A workspace states which putnami engine may run against it, and a workspace that builds its own engine refuses every binary it did not produce

features.name: Collaboration provider routing
features.outcome: A workspace binds its task, change-proposal, memory and missions backends independently, and a user, a script or an agent calls the same versioned operations through the CLI or MCP without knowing which backend answers, while a missing binding or capability, a refused precondition and an uncertain write are stated rather than hidden

features.name: Contributor workflows
features.outcome: A workspace uses build to carry its requested outcome, issue or epic through delivery planning, bounded experiments, independent artifact challenge and verified delivery on both supported hosts, with native requirement coverage, portable records, canonical entry points and proof-consuming Go publication under its existing mandate and provider policy

features.name: Windows consumer install and golden path
features.outcome: A user on Windows 10 version 1803 or later or Windows 11, on amd64, installs the CLI with one PowerShell line that verifies what it downloads and needs no administrator rights, then initializes and serves the TypeScript starter as on macOS and Linux, with every Windows prerequisite named where it is missing

features.name: Credential provider for registry downloads
features.outcome: A user who turns on --providers install gets the archive downloads of that process authenticated by the workspace's one credential provider, asked once per purpose and sent only to the hosts its credential names, while a workspace without a provider behaves as before

features.name: Credential custody on hosted runs
features.outcome: A hosted runner that passes the run credential on --credential-fd gets a run in which no repository-controlled process can read a credential, and a cold install of a private pin that works from an empty store, while a run without the flag behaves as before

features.name: Init resolves on one channel
features.outcome: A user who runs putnami init or putnami projects create on a release channel gets extensions, a template and starter dependencies that all come from that channel, and the workspace pins no channel

features.name: First-use path on a bare machine
features.outcome: A new user on macOS or Linux pastes the documented block into a shell that holds only Bash, curl, tar and a SHA-256 tool, and gets a served starter; each release proves that block, the checks and the Go path in an image that holds nothing else

features.name: Publication through providers
features.outcome: A user who publishes, locally or on a hosted runner, gets a run whose ancestry and publish credential are fixed before any repository code runs, whose uploads and channel release go through one credential provider session, and in which neither the engine nor a repository process holds a publish credential, while a run or a bound request that only gates starts no publication

features.name: Workspace without git
features.outcome: A user builds, tests and serves a workspace in a directory Git does not manage, and every command that needs git history refuses in one line that names git and the command to run

features.name: Publish dry-run registry probe
features.outcome: A user learns from one publish --dry-run which planned members a registry would refuse, before any member is written

features.name: Impact plan
features.outcome: An extension asks the engine for the impacted plan of a change, for the commands it names, and reads it with the protocol package alone

features.name: Extension dependencies
features.outcome: Declaring an extension installs, pins and loads every extension it depends on, so the dependency graph decides what a workspace gets

features.name: Supervised serve run
features.outcome: A supervisor starts a workload with one putnami serve run, hands its serve step the process environment the workload needs on stdin, and reads from the session stream which process group the workload runs in and when it is ready, however many ordinary log lines the workload writes
